nativeEvidence.establishes: Reachable new/edit form exposes All-day, Starts and Ends date/time rows; end range starts at startDate, changing start preserves nonnegative duration. Custom menu navigates to recurrence editor. Repeat presets daily/weekly/monthly/yearly plus every2weeks; End Repeat Never/On Date. Timed persistence max(end,start), not automatic next-day inference. All-day stores inclusive UI end with next-day boundary. Event timezone comes from saved local/EK event or device fallback. Save requires title and editable selected calendar; recurring existing EK save uses futureEvents, no scope prompt established here.

Separate date/time value buttons; date opens CalendarInlineDateGrid with range, time opens bounded wheel picker. Supports explicit endpoint date selection. Does not infer shift type or employer roster.
Daily/weekly/monthly/yearly frequency, interval control1…999, weekly weekday selection; monthly/yearly pattern options. General recurrence editor, no shift-template selector in inspected controls.

Builds EKRecurrenceRule with interval and selected day dimensions. Can preserve original rule dimensions when unedited; this does not prove every exception survives arbitrary edits or every provider uses identical results.

supportedBoundedAdvice: For an overnight timed shift, keep All-day off, choose the correct start date/time and explicitly choose the next date for the end time.
Example: an agreed Monday22:00–Tuesday06:00 shift must have Tuesday as the ending date; a clock-only06:00 on Monday is not the intended interval.
Reopen the saved event and check both dates/times, destination and relevant time zone. Do not infer correct duration solely from a grid block.
Use Repeat only when a regular rule actually matches the agreed roster. Check representative later occurrences before relying on it.
For a one-date change, use an editor that explicitly supports the intended scope; do not assume a Cloud scope prompt.
An irregular or revised roster can be recorded as explicitly dated shifts rather than forcing an unsuitable repeat rule. This is a manual planning suggestion, not a tested bulk-entry feature.

proposedTargetedAddition.heading: Set both dates before repeating an overnight shift
body: For an agreed shift from Monday at 22:00 to Tuesday at 06:00, create a timed event and set the ending date to Tuesday. In Cloud Calendars, Starts and Ends include date choices as well as times. Read both endpoints before saving; entering an earlier clock time on the same date is not the same as specifying an overnight shift.

Check that first saved shift before choosing a repeat pattern. Use a regular rule only when it matches the confirmed roster, then inspect the next occurrence and a date where the schedule changes. For a one-off swap, use an editor that explicitly supports the required occurrence scope. A calendar entry does not approve the swap, calculate pay or establish another person’s availability.

newPageDecision.reason: There is a concrete missing overnight example, but the verified controls and surrounding checks fit the existing recurrence guide without creating a generic shift-keyword duplicate. A separate page would need a genuinely distinct multi-step roster workflow and primary evidence for its extra claims; no rotating-template product capability was established.
